## Objective

Deliver the release through existing mapping and receipt mechanisms without adopting real products.

## Scope

- Neutral starter and Template publication
- New-project specialization
- Prior-edition adoption and refresh
- Preservation/recovery fixtures

## Entry conditions

- The preceding phase has accepted artifacts and current passing evidence.

## Exit criteria

- Every phase task meets its criteria and planned verification with current evidence; relevant preservation checks pass.

## Risks

- Edition tables can accidentally move earlier learning/memory contracts when SETUP_CONTRACT changes; retain explicit v5/v6/v7 membership.
- Whole-package customization must stop a merge rather than create a false ready installation.

### Risks

- Preserve unrelated bytes and stop on stale inputs or a scope conflict.

### Acceptance criteria

- Neutral identity and authority are unset until specialization; the Template package contains no root instances, grants, learned records, links or generated graph/wiki/runtime.
- The existing schema-2 starter policy retains its keys; exact starter_files and bounded reference-assets entries select the new capability.
- The updater uses ordinary collection/skill discovery; engine changes are unnecessary unless current evidence reveals a required conflict.

### Planned verification

- Validate the complete starter inventory and source mapping in a disposable depot before any real Template apply.
- Scan neutral package contents for root identity, absolute private paths, runtime and publication data; verify locked module hashes.

### Acceptance criteria

- A plain rerun preserves its base edition and adds no ontology; selected adoption retains source/destination identities, exact versions, overwrite boundaries and archived base receipt.

- Use customized, incomplete and incompatible fixtures and assert preserved content plus accurate readiness diagnostics.
